summary.headline: ENIL Q2 FY27 domestic revenue fell 16.1% YoY to INR114 crores, while EBITDA rose 9.5% to INR11.3 crores on cost cuts and lower digital losses.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR117 crores including INR3 crores from international operations, with domestic revenue down 16.1% YoY to INR114 crores. Management blamed subdued advertising demand in radio and a festive shift that pushed event and advertising revenue into Q3. EBITDA still rose 9.5% YoY to INR11.3 crores on structural cost measures and a smaller digital loss. Digital EBITDA loss narrowed 23.3% to INR7.5 crores, and consolidated cash stood at INR371.5 crores at 30 September 2026, down from INR424 crores in March 2026.

segments.name: Radio (FCT)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 12.6% YoY to about INR60 crores; radio is about 53% of domestic revenue. Inventory utilisation about 70%, down about 6%; volumes down about 5% and effective rates flat. Management cites roughly 25% radio market share.

segments.name: Non-FCT (events and other)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR20 crores, weighed by festive calendar shift as events moved into Q3. EBITDA margin 30.8% vs 27.8% a year ago. Management says event margins will stay below radio margins, with rising competition from TV, news and internet players.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: About 29% of domestic revenue vs 23% a year ago. Gaana revenue about INR22 crores (ballpark). Digital EBITDA loss INR7.5 crores vs INR9.8 crores. Gaana EBITDA breakeven target is Q4 FY27, which management says could slip 1-2 quarters on higher subscriber acquisition costs.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; it said it is seeing green shoots in advertising in Q3 FY27 and expects them to continue.
Gaana EBITDA breakeven remains the ambition for Q4 FY27, but could be delayed by 1-2 quarters because of higher acquisition costs.
Cash decline was described as seasonal (vendor advances for events, dividend, digital tech capex) and expected to recover to earlier levels.
Management expects radio advertising to stay subdued near term and is focused on cost structure and profitability rather than revenue growth alone.
Management is in discussions with the government on radio reforms and expects them, linked to the new frequency licence investment question.
capex_capacity: Radio inventory utilisation about 70%, down about 6%; volumes down about 5%.
Events: more than 200-250 events a year across 63 markets; management says it is selectively investing in events.
Digital tech capex was made in the quarter, contributing to the cash decline.
Management flagged the 15-year radio licence fees and a 2029 renewal, and said it would bid for licences on renewal.
demand_pricing: Radio advertising demand remained subdued; FCT revenue down 12.6% YoY.
Radio effective rates were flat YoY; volumes were down about 5%.
Event competition increased over the last 6-9 months from TV, news and internet companies, pressuring margins.
Gaana acquisition costs rose as AI search reduced referral traffic and Google performance marketing became more expensive.
Management said some Q2 event revenue moved into Q3 because Diwali fell later this year.

qa_highlights.question: Can you split core radio and non-radio revenue for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Radio was about INR60 crores, down about 12%; non-radio (events) was INR20 crores, excluding digital.

qa_highlights.question: What were inventory utilisation and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory utilisation was about 70%, down about 6%. Effective rates were flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current assets rise on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Sanjay Ballabh said it was due to accumulation of prepaid items in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the return on capital weak given radio licence fees, and will ENIL bid at the 2029 renewal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said radio is an efficient last-mile medium, that it is in talks with government on reforms, and that the radio share is 53% of domestic revenue and may be under 50% on a full-year basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is digital revenue flat from September 2025 to September 2026 (INR32 crores, 31, 29, 31, 33 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital grew continuously; ENIL is not chasing Gaana subscriber numbers and is managing unit economics. Gaana revenue is about INR22 crores in the quarter, and Digital Solutions and Gaana are the two large digital businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cash fall from INR424 crores (March 2026) to INR371 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited advances to vendors for events, dividend payment and digital tech capex; it said the decline is seasonal and cash should recover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did existing business fall about 25% YoY (INR104 crores to INR81 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to subdued advertising, and to events being pushed into Q3 by the later Diwali, which left events down largely due to the festive shift.

risks_watch: Subdued radio advertising and rising competition in events may keep top-line pressure through Q3 FY27.
Gaana EBITDA breakeven target (Q4 FY27) may slip 1-2 quarters on higher subscriber acquisition costs.
Radio licence renewal (2029) economics and the timing of government reforms remain unclear.
Cash balance trend (INR371.5 crores) needs to recover as management expects; watch Q3 figures.
Investor disclosure was criticised: the investor deck dropped FCT/non-FCT splits, and management has not reconciled the digital revenue series raised by analysts.
summary.management_tone: Management is cautious on revenue, attributing the decline to subdued advertising, geopolitics and the festive shift, but confident on profitability and cost action. It was evasive on the digital revenue series and on Gaana subscriber numbers, offering to share figures later, and it did not give formal guidance.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 was a mixed quarter for ENIL.
We believe this evolution is important in positioning ENIL as a more diversified media and entertainment company with opportunities extending well beyond traditional radio.
So, we do not chase numbers, but chase profitable growth, and that's what we continue to do.
Event margins will never be similar to radio margins.

financial_highlights.change: Loss reduced 23.3% YoY from INR9.8 crores
Down from INR409 crores in June 2026 and INR424 crores in March 2026

growth.why: No formal guidance; management expects radio ad demand to stay subdued near term (FCT revenue -12.6%, volumes -5%, utilisation ~70% and down ~6%), with Gaana EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 now possibly slipping 1-2 quarters and focus on cost and profitability rather than revenue growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Non-FCT EBITDA margin rose to 30.8% from 27.8% and digital loss narrowed 23.3% to INR7.5 crores on cost actions, but event margins will stay below radio and internet entrants add pressure, and Gaana breakeven may slip 1-2 quarters from Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Radio inventory utilisation is about 70% and down about 6%, with volumes down about 5%, so there is no sign of new radio capacity needed; events are being invested in selectively.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FCT revenue fell 12.6% YoY to about INR60 crores with volumes down about 5% and effective rates flat, and management expects radio ad demand to stay subdued near term, with green shoots only expected in Q3 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 70% and falling, so there is no capacity squeeze to force a new capex announcement; digital tech capex was already made in the quarter.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal guidance was given, and top-line commentary is cautious with radio FCT revenue down 12.6% YoY and domestic revenue down 16.1%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management has already said Gaana EBITDA breakeven, the Q4 FY27 ambition, could slip 1-2 quarters on higher subscriber acquisition costs, and radio demand is expected to stay subdued near term.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed in the call.

rows.label: Radio reforms and 2029 licence renewal
rows.why: Management is in talks with government on radio reforms, but timing is unclear and radio share is 53% of domestic revenue, possibly under 50% on a full-year basis, with the 2029 renewal economics unresolved.

rows.label: Structural cost measures and digital loss reduction
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA rose 9.5% YoY to INR11.3 crores on structural cost measures, and the digital EBITDA loss narrowed to INR7.5 crores from INR9.8 crores (down 23.3%).

rows.label: Cash recovery from INR371.5 crores
rows.why: Cash fell from INR424 crores in March 2026 to INR371.5 crores, which management calls seasonal (event vendor advances, dividend, digital capex) and expects to recover, though other current assets rose on prepaid items.

tone.note: Management was cautious on radio and event revenue, citing subdued ad demand and the festive shift, but confident on cost and profitability; analysts pressed on the digital revenue series and Gaana subscribers, which management was evasive about.
